writer_fixes: FIXED: encode_layer_block() — ec@92 changed from 0 to 1 (matches native: always 1 when geometry exists — it's a 'has geometry' flag, not element count)
FIXED: header() — last layer block offset606 changed from hardcoded 1 to actual element count = sum(len(layer._paths) across all layers)
BOTH FIXES were discovered by cross-referencing native VCF hex dumps with vcf_parser_b2b production parser code — the B2B parser reads offset606 for element enumeration
analytical_discoveries: DISCOVERED (off-by-2): POST_STOCK_HEADER = 14B (4B uint32 + 8B float64 + 2B uint16), not 12B. This off-by-2 shifted all layer block field analysis.
DISCOVERED (ec@92 semantics): ec@92 = 1 in ALL native files (1-elem and 2-elem). It is a boolean 'has geometry' flag, NOT element count.
DISCOVERED (offset606 semantics): offset606 in last layer block = total element count across all layers. Verified against all 4 native multi-element files.

DISCOVERED (B2B parser architecture): vcf_parser_b2b uses GEOMETRY_SIG forward scan + backward block scan for parsing. It does NOT read ec@92 or offset606 at all. It reads GEOMETRY_SIG markers and counts geometry sections directly.

DISCOVERED (parser vs GUI gap): Production parser always found correct element count even before our fixes — because it scans binary structure. GUI uses offset606. Both are valid but different mechanisms.
